context: Matched to the live Full Application Draft for Nik Horner, Illinois District 11 (Bill Foster). Answers, cover, and public Vimeo link saved and verified after reopening. Final readiness remains unchecked; no final submission performed.

fields.prompt: What is your app called?
Which programming language(s) did you use to create your app?
fields.answer: Select JavaScript. HTML and CSS can be named in the written description as markup and styling technologies.

fields.prompt: Which platform(s) did you code your app for?
Please list the link to your app's video demonstration here
Please briefly describe what your app does?
fields.answer:
TrueLine is free, open-source desktop tracing software for makers. It helps turn physical parts and part images into editable, scaled 2D CAD outlines. Users can trace with a mouse or pen tablet, review fitted lines and curves, or create a circle by picking three points around its edge. They can set the drawing’s scale from a known measurement and use optional image outline detection as another starting point.

Drawings can be saved and exported as DXF, SVG, or PDF for fabrication, repair, and pattern making. Processing stays on the user’s device. Users must verify edges and dimensions before fabrication.

fields.prompt: What inspired you to create this app?
fields.answer: My dad and I had a physical part but no CAD model for it. We tried taking a picture and tracing it in SolidWorks, but that did not work well for us. We found a paid solution that cost about $1,500. That experience inspired TrueLine: a free tool focused on tracing, reviewing the outline, and setting its scale before exporting it. I built and refined the tracing functionality and tested it with parts.

fields.prompt: What technical difficulties did you face programming your app?
fields.answer:
One challenge was turning a traced curve into useful CAD geometry. An arc should stay an arc, rather than becoming thousands of tiny line segments. I built and refined the tracing functionality to fit suitable strokes as lines, circles, and arcs, with smoothing and a preview before acceptance.

Earlier image-processing approaches also struggled with more complicated parts. Using my machine-learning knowledge, I helped move the image-tracing approach to a small pretrained neural network. The app now uses MobileSAM with local inference, followed by edge processing and editable outlines. I tested the results and refined the tracing behavior; users still need to review the outline and verify measurements.

fields.prompt: What improvements would you make if you were to create a 2.0 version of your app?
fields.answer: I would improve photo tracing for difficult lighting and backgrounds, make uncertain edges easier to review, and test it with more real parts. I would also make it easier for a new user to verify scale with a second known measurement before exporting.
fields.note: Proposed product direction for the creator to review.

fields.prompt: Did you use AI in the creation, development, or functionality of your app?
If you used AI, tell us how you used it and what your team contributed directly.
fields.answer:
I used Codex and Claude Code for implementation, debugging, and testing assistance; AI generated much of the app's code. My direct work focused on building and refining the tracing functionality, especially representing curves as CAD arcs rather than many short line segments. I also used my machine-learning knowledge to help choose a small neural-network approach when earlier image processing struggled with complicated parts, and tested and refined the results.

TrueLine uses the existing pretrained MobileSAM model through ONNX Runtime Web for local image segmentation; I did not train that model. Codex also helped with bug fixes, tests, demo production, and drafting these submission materials.

fields.prompt: What did you learn or take away from participating in the Congressional App Challenge?
fields.answer: The tracing problem taught me that more points and edges do not automatically produce a better CAD drawing. The geometry needs to represent the intended shape, and an arc should remain a usable arc. Testing the output helped me identify what needed to improve.
